label: 胡金铨武侠 · King Hu (Come Drink with Me → A Touch of Zen)
source: Harvard Film Archive and BFI programme notes; David Bordwell's account of 'the glimpse' — bursts of six-frame shots that register as movement rather than as images. Peking-opera choreography, real locations, bamboo and mist.

look.image: King Hu wuxia frame: real mountain location, tall bamboo grove with shafts of hard sunlight cutting through, natural haze and dust in the air, muted earth and ink-wash palette with one accent of costume colour, Ming-dynasty robes and scholar's dress, figures small against landscape, composition balanced like a scroll painting, 1970s Taiwanese location film stock, restrained grain
look.video: Peking-opera derived combat: a figure springs, is glimpsed mid-air for an instant, and lands elsewhere in the frame; bamboo sways and slashes past the lens; dust and leaves hang in the light
look.negatives: soundstage backdrop, neon, modern clothing, glossy digital sheen, heavy colour gels, slow-motion, orange-and-teal grading, CGI creatures

camera.clause: brief, decisive framing — the move ends before the eye settles

pacing.note: The glimpse: action is assembled from very short shots, some a quarter of a second, while spatial continuity is preserved. Ask for shorter shots than the genre default.

notes: Opposite of Shaw on colour: desaturated, natural light, real locations. The energy comes from cutting, not from the palette — so the pack pushes contrast and pulls saturation.
